issues.legal_issue: The general land acquisition procedure remains available for acquiring land for a trust despite a special town-planning law that incorporates that procedure with modifications.
material_facts: A town-planning law established an improvement trust and provided that the general land acquisition procedure, as modified by a schedule, would apply to acquisitions for the trust.
The State Government issued acquisition notifications for land at the trust’s expense for a housing and planned-development purpose after the town-planning law had come into force.
The High Court quashed the notifications on the ground that the special law displaced the general acquisition procedure, and the trust appealed.
issues.conclusion: The special law did not exclude the general land acquisition procedure. The State Government’s notifications were not invalid merely because they were issued under that procedure after the special law came into force; the High Court’s order was set aside and the matter remitted for consideration of an unresolved constitutional challenge.
issues.legal_principle: The special law’s provision applying the Land Acquisition Act subject to scheduled modifications, including the substitution of specified trust-scheme steps for steps under sections 4, 5-A and 6, showed that the general acquisition machinery remained applicable rather than being excluded. The provision on master plans contemplated compulsory acquisition by the State Government, and the Land Acquisition Act’s section 50(1) remained available for acquisitions for a trust. The Court referred to Mercer Henderson’s Trustees v. Dunferuline District Committee, 37 Sc. L.R. 119, in construing the words “previously made.”

predicates.appeal_from_quashing_of_acquisition_noti: An appeal challenges a judgment that quashed a government acquisition notice.
predicates.acquisition_for_trust_purpose: The land was proposed to be acquired for a trust’s purpose.
predicates.special_law_adopts_modified_general_acqu: The special law provides that the general acquisition procedure applies to trust acquisitions subject to specified modifications.
predicates.special_law_allows_state_compulsory_acqu: The special law contemplates compulsory acquisition by the State Government.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the quashing of a government notice for a trust acquisition, the special law adopts the general procedure with modifications, and the special law contemplates State compulsory acquisition, the notice is not invalid merely because the special law is in force.

issues.legal_issue: A general acquisition notice made and in force before the first publication of a trust-scheme notice is not displaced by that later scheme notice, even if the general notice was made after the special law came into force.
material_facts: The special law provided that the first publication of a trust-scheme notice would ordinarily take the place of a general acquisition notification, subject to an exception for a general acquisition notification or declaration previously made and in force.
The Court construed “previously made” as referring to a notice made before the first publication of the trust-scheme notice, not only one made before the special law came into force.
issues.conclusion: A general acquisition notification or declaration made and in force before the first publication of a trust-scheme notice falls within the exception, whether it was issued before or after the special law came into force.
issues.legal_principle: Under the schedule modifying the Land Acquisition Act, the first publication of a notice under section 46 ordinarily substituted for a notification under section 4(1), except where a section 4(1) notification or section 6 declaration had been previously made and was in force. The Court held that “previously made” meant made before the first publication of the scheme notice, and referred to Mercer Henderson’s Trustees v. Dunferuline District Committee, 37 Sc. L.R. 119, in construing comparable language.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a trust land acquisition and a general acquisition notice was made before, and remains in force at, the first publication of the trust-scheme notice, that earlier notice is not replaced by the later scheme notice.
